# onetsolutions_web_hosting (Resource)

Manages an OnetSolutions web hosting, a billed order on its billing cycle.

~> **Billing.** Creating this resource **places an order**: the web hosting is billed on its
`billing_cycle` (monthly or longer) from the moment it is ordered. With `domain_source = "register"`
or `"transfer"`, the domain is billed on the same order, and a registration cannot be undone. A
plan change is an upgrade order too, applied once paid. `terraform plan` shows the price of each
order as a warning, and refuses a plan that is not on sale or a billing cycle it is not sold on.

!> **Destroying cancels at the end of the billing period.** Neither `terraform destroy` nor a
change that replaces the web hosting (`domain`) deletes it: both request its cancellation at the
end of the current billing period, with `cancellation_reason_code` and `cancellation_reason`. The
web hosting **keeps running and is billed until `next_billing_date`**, then it is closed with its
files, databases and e-mail. The resource leaves the state at once, with a warning giving that
date, so a replacement bills the old web hosting and the new one side by side until then. A domain
registered or transferred with it is not cancelled. To keep the web hosting, revoke the
cancellation in the console before that date and import it again. `deletion_protection = true`
refuses the destroy.

## Changes

`plan_id` changes in place through an upgrade order, to a plan the web hosting is eligible to
(checked at plan time), with `billing_cycle` if it changes too: the cycle can only change with a
new plan, and only to a longer cycle. The apply waits until the new plan applies, which happens
once its invoice is paid. `deletion_protection`, `cancellation_reason_code` and
`cancellation_reason` change in place without any request. Only `domain` replaces the web hosting.

`domain_source` and `epp_code` are sent by the order only. Changing one later does not replace the
web hosting: the new value is stored in the state with a plan-time warning. After an import they
are taken from the configuration without a warning.

## Unpaid orders

The web hosting exists as soon as it is ordered, with status `pending`. When the account balance
does not cover the order, the apply ends with a warning giving the order, its invoice and the
payment link, and the web hosting stays in the state, `pending`: applying again orders nothing.
It is set up once the invoice is paid, and the next refresh reads it `active`. Until then, its
PHP versions and WordPress sites cannot be managed.

## Cancellation requested outside Terraform

A web hosting cancelled in the console stays in the state: the refresh fills
`cancellation_requested_at`, warns that the web hosting ends at the end of its billing period, and
plans nothing. Once it is terminated (`status` is `terminated` or `cancelled`), it leaves the
state, and the next plan orders a new one: remove it from the configuration to let it end, or
revoke the cancellation to keep it.

## Timeouts and failures

If the response to an order is lost (timeout, server error), the apply stops without recording
anything in the state: check the console before applying again.

A create that fails or times out once the web hosting exists keeps it in the state, marked
**tainted**: the next apply would replace it, which cancels it and orders a new one. To keep it,
wait until it is active and run `terraform untaint` on its address. A plan change that times out
(its invoice unpaid) leaves the current plan in the state; the plan changes once the invoice is
paid, and a second change is refused until then. Right after an order, a destroy waits until the
web hosting can be cancelled, within the `delete` timeout.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_hosting_plans" "all" {}

locals {
  business = one([for p in data.onetsolutions_hosting_plans.all.plans : p if p.slug == "hebergement-business"])
}

# Creating this resource places an order billed on billing_cycle. Destroying it requests its
# cancellation at the end of the billing period: it keeps running, and billed, until then.
resource "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain        = "example.fr"
  plan_id       = local.business.id
  billing_cycle = "annually"

  # The domain is registered elsewhere and pointed at the web hosting's name servers.
  domain_source = "external"

  deletion_protection = true

  # Sent with the cancellation once deletion_protection is lifted and the resource destroyed.
  cancellation_reason_code = "no_longer_needed"
  cancellation_reason      = "This site moves to a larger plan of another account."
}

output "nameservers" {
  value = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.nameservers
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The primary domain of the web hosting, such as `example.com`: lowercase, without a trailing dot. Changing it replaces the web hosting.
- `plan_id` (String) The UUID of the plan (see `onetsolutions_hosting_plans`). Can be changed in place to a plan the web hosting is eligible to (checked at plan time): the change is an upgrade order, applied once paid.

### Optional

- `billing_cycle` (String) The billing cycle, one of `free`, `one_time`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annually`, `annually`, `biennially`, `triennially`. When unset, `monthly` for a new web hosting, and the current cycle afterwards. `free` and `one_time` exist only on web hostings already billed that way, such as imported ones. The cycle changes only together with a new `plan_id`, and only to a longer cycle.
- `cancellation_reason` (String) A sentence of at least 7 words explaining the cancellation, sent with `cancellation_reason_code` when the resource is destroyed or replaced. When unset, a default sentence is recorded. Sent only by the destroy: a change is stored without any request.
- `cancellation_reason_code` (String) Why the web hosting is cancelled when the resource is destroyed or replaced, one of `too_expensive`, `no_longer_needed`, `missing_feature`, `technical_issue`, `switching_provider`, `other`. Defaults to `no_longer_needed`. Sent only by the destroy: a change is stored without any request, so set it and apply before destroying.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the web hosting is refused. Defaults to `false`. Set it to `false` and apply before destroying a protected web hosting.
- `domain_source` (String) Where `domain` comes from, applied by the order only: `external` (a domain registered elsewhere, pointed at the web hosting), `existing` (a domain of the organization), `register` (registers the domain, billed on the same order) or `transfer` (transfers it in with `epp_code`, billed on the same order). When unset, `external`. A later change is stored with a plan-time warning and has no effect.
- `epp_code` (String, Sensitive) The transfer code of the domain, required with `domain_source = "transfer"` and refused otherwise. Sent by the order only.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `bandwidth_limit_mb` (Number) The monthly bandwidth allowed, in MB; 0 means unlimited.
- `cancellation_requested_at` (String) When a cancellation at the end of the billing period was requested (RFC 3339), null when none is. Set by a destroy, or by a cancellation requested in the console: the web hosting then stays in the state, unchanged, until it ends.
- `created` (String) When the web hosting was created (RFC 3339).
- `dedicated_ip` (String) The dedicated IP address, null when none is assigned.
- `disk_limit_mb` (Number) The disk space allowed, in MB.
- `id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting.
- `nameservers` (List of String) The name servers to delegate the domain to.
- `next_billing_date` (String) The next renewal date (RFC 3339), null when none is scheduled.
- `plan_name` (String) The name of the plan.
- `price` (String) The price per billing cycle, in EUR excluding tax, as a decimal string.
- `status` (String) `pending` (ordered, being set up or awaiting payment), `active`, `suspended`, `terminated`, `cancelled` or `failed`.
- `username` (String) The account's login name, empty until the web hosting is set up.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `30m`.
- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the deletion, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `30m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<id>, or <id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
# domain_source and epp_code are taken from the configuration after an import, without a warning.
terraform import onetsolutions_web_hosting.site 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f
```
